questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has $1\muF$ capacitance. One of its two plates is given $+ 2\muC$ charge and the other plate, $+ 4\muC$ charge. The potential difference developed across the capacitor is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Charge inside capacitor $= 1\muC$
$V = \dfrac{Q}{C} = \dfrac{1 \times {10}^{- 6}}{1 \times {10}^{- 6}} = 1$ volt

questions.q: Two capacitors of capacitances $C$ and $2C$~are charged to potential differences $V$ and $2V$, respectively. These are then connected in parallel in such a manner that the positive terminal of one is connected to the negative terminal of the other. The final energy of this configuration is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Charge on $C = CV$
Charge on $2C = \left(2C\right)2V$

From charge conservation, $2C ( 2V ) - CV = ( C + 2C ) V '$
Common potential,~$V ' = V$
Final energy,~${U}_{f} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2CV^{2}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2}CV^{2}$

questions.q: A parallel-plate capacitor with plate area $A$ has separation $d$ between the plates. Two dielectric slabs of dielectric constant ${K}_{1}$ and ${K}_{2}$ of same area $\dfrac{A}{2}$~and thickness $\dfrac{d}{2}$& are inserted in the space between the plates. The capacitance of the capacitor will be given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${C}_{eq} = {C}_{1} + \dfrac{{C}_{2}{C}_{3}}{{C}_{2} + {C}_{3}}$

${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{2d} + \dfrac{\dfrac{{K}_{1}A{ε}_{0}}{d} \times \dfrac{{K}_{2}A{ε}_{0}}{d}}{\dfrac{{K}_{1}A{ε}_{0}}{d} + \dfrac{{K}_{2}A{ε}_{0}}{d}}$

${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{2d} + \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{d}\left(\dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}}\right) = \dfrac{A{ε}_{0}}{d} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}}\right)

$

questions.q: Two capacitors having capacitance ${C}_{1}$~and ${C}_{2}$ respectively are connected as shown in figure. Initially, capacitor ${C}_{1}$ is charged to a potential difference $V$ volt by a battery. The battery is then removed and the charged capacitor ${C}_{1}$ is now connected to uncharged capacitor ${C}_{2}$ by closing the switch $S$. The amount of charge on the capacitor ${C}_{2}$, after equilibrium, is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The initial charge on the capacitor& ${C}_{1}$~will be~$Q = {C}_{1}V$. If after closing the~ switch the charge flown through the circuit is~$q$, the charge on~${C}_{2}$~will be~$q$~and~${C}_{1}$~will be~$Q - q$. The potential across the capacitors will be same. Hence,

$\dfrac{Q - q}{C1} = \dfrac{q}{C2} ⇒ q = \dfrac{{C}_{2}Q}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}} ⇒ q = \dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}V$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $1 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is charged to a potential difference of 20 V . The distance between plates is $1 \mu \mathrm{~m}$. The energy density between plates of capacitor is.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \text { Energy density } & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0 E^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2} \varepsilon_0\left(\frac{V}{d}\right)^2 \\ & =\frac{1}{2}\left(8.85 \times 10^{-12}\right)\left(\frac{20}{10^{-6}}\right)^2 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^3 \\ & \simeq 1.8 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{m}^3\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A bulb and a capacitor are connected in series across an ac supply. A dielectric is then placed between the plates of the capacitor. The glow of the bulb:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2} \ \text{ and } X_C=\frac{1}{W C}$ due to dielectric $\mathrm{C} \uparrow \Rightarrow \mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}} \downarrow \Rightarrow \mathrm{Z} \downarrow$ So, current increases $\ \text{ and } $ thus bulb will glow more brighter.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $100\mu F$ is charged to a potential of $12V$ and connected to a $6 . 4mH$ inductor to produce oscillations. The maximum current in the circuit would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By energy conservation, it follows that

$\dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}L{I}_\max^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation (1) implies that

\begin{cases}{I}_\max$& = & $\sqrt{\dfrac{C}{L}}$V \\ & = & $\sqrt{\dfrac{100 \times {10}^{- 6}}{6 . 4 \times {10}^{- 3}}} \times$12 \\ & = & $\dfrac{12}{8}$\\ & = & 1 . 5A\end{cases}

$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $C$ is charged to a potential $V$. The flux of the electric field through a closed surface enclosing the positive plate of the capacitor is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
& The charge enclosed is given by& ${q}_{inc} = CV$ ~

Gauss' law states that the flux through any closed surface is equal to the charge enclosed by the surface.

~Using Gauss' law the flux is, $ϕ = \dfrac{q\text{inc}}{ε0} = \left(\dfrac{CV}{ε0}\right)

$

questions.q: Three capacitors ${C}_{1} = 2\muF, {C}_{2} = 6\muF$ and ${C}_{3} = 12\muF$ are connected as shown in the figure. Find the ratio of the charges on capacitors ${C}_{1}, {C}_{2}$ and ${C}_{3}$ respectively.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From the above circuit diagram, the equivalent capacitance of the combination of capacitors is,&

${C}_{eq} = {C}_{1} + \dfrac{{C}_{2}{C}_{3}}{{C}_{2}{C}_{3}}$,~

${C}_{eq} = 2 + \dfrac{6 \times 12}{6 + 12} = 6\muF$

Then,~$\dfrac{Q{C}_{1}}{Q{C}_{2}} = \dfrac{{C}_{1}V}{\dfrac{{C}_{2}{C}_{3}}{{C}_{2} + {C}_{3}}V} = \dfrac{2 \times ( 6 + 12 )}{6 \times 12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$~

and~${Q}_{C2} = {Q}_{C3}$

So, the ratio of charges are,~$1: 2: 2$.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with square plates is filled with four dielectrics of dielectric constants ${K}_{1}, {K}_{2}, {K}_{3}, {K}_{4}$ arranged as shown in the figure. The effective dielectric constant $K$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ are in series.

The equivalent capacitance of ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ is

${C}_{12} = \dfrac{{\in}_{0}\dfrac{A}{2}}{\dfrac{d}{2{K}_{1}} + \dfrac{d}{2{K}_{2}}} = \dfrac{{\in}_{0}A}{d}\dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}}$

${C}_{3}\text{and}{C}_{4}\text{are in series}$

${C}_{34} = \dfrac{{\in}_{0}\dfrac{A}{2}}{\dfrac{d}{2{K}_{3}} + \dfrac{d}{2{K}_{4}}} = \dfrac{{\in}_{0}A}{d}\dfrac{{K}_{3}{K}_{4}}{{K}_{3} + {K}_{4}}$

${C}_{eq} = {C}_{12} + {C}_{34} = \dfrac{{\in}_{0}A}{d} \left(\dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}} + \dfrac{{K}_{3}{K}_{4}}{{K}_{3} + {K}_{4}}\right)

$∴ {K}_{eq} = \left(\dfrac{{K}_{1}{K}_{2}}{{K}_{1} + {K}_{2}} + \dfrac{{K}_{3} . {K}_{4}}{{K}_{3} + {K}_{4}}\right)$

$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor filled with a medium of dielectric constant $10$, is connected across a battery and is charged. The dielectric slab is replaced by another slab of dielectric constant $15$. Then the energy of capacitor will
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a dielectric of dielectric constant& $K$~is inserted between the plates of a capacitor~${C}_{0}$, the capacitance becomes~$K{C}_{0}$.

Energy stored in a capacitor is given by,~$U = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2}$. Now,

${U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({K}_{1}{C}_{0}\right)V^{2}$~and~${U}_{f} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({K}_{2}{C}_{0}\right)V^{2}$

$⇒ \Delta U = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({K}_{2} - {K}_{1}\right){C}_{0}V^{2}$

Percentage change in the energy will be,

$\dfrac{\Delta U}{Ui} \times 100 = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times {C0}^{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2} \times 10 \times {C0}^{2}} \times 100 = 50 %$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Two metallic spheres are charged to the same potential. One of them is hollow and another is solid, and both have the same radii. Solid sphere will have lower charge than the hollow one.

Reason R : Capacitance of metallic spheres depend on the radii of spheres.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential of a conducting sphere is given by& $V = \dfrac{KQ}{R}$~

As in case of metallic sphere either solid or hollow, the charge will reside on the surface of the sphere. Since both spheres have same surface area, so they can hold equal charge.

$∴ {Q}_{1} = {Q}_{2}$

The capacitance of a metallic sphere depends only on its radius. It does not matter whether the sphere is hollow or solid.

Hence,& A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Effective capacitance of parallel combination of two capacitors ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ is $10\muF .$ When these capacitors are individually connected to a voltage source of $1V,$ the energy stored in the capacitor ${C}_{2}$ is $4$ times that of ${C}_{1} .$ If these capacitors are connected in series, their effective capacitance will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given ${C}_{1} + {C}_{2} = 10\muF$ ...(i)
$4\left(\dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{1}V^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}{C}_{2}V^{2}$
$⇒ 4{C}_{1} = {C}_{2}$...(ii)
From equation (i) and (ii)
${C}_{1} = 2\muF$
${C}_{2} = 8\muF$
If they are in series
${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1}{+}_{2}} = 1.6\muF$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has plate area $40{cm}^{2}$ and plates separation $2$ mm. The space between the plates is filled with a dielectric medium of a thickness $1$ mm and dielectric constant $5$. The capacitance of the system is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
With insertion of dielectric, the system can& be considered as combination of two capacitors in series.

Thus, equivalent capacitance of the system is&

$\dfrac{1}{Ceq} = \dfrac{1}{C1} + \dfrac{1}{C2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{K{ε}_{0}At} + \dfrac{1}{{ε}_{0}Ad - t}$

$= \dfrac{t}{K{ε}_{0}A} + \dfrac{d - t}{{ε}_{0}A}$

$= \dfrac{1 \times {10}^{- 3}}{5{ε}_{0} \times 40 \times {10}^{- 4}} + \dfrac{1 \times {10}^{- 3}}{{ε}_{0} \times 40 \times {10}^{- 4}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{Ceq} = \dfrac{1}{20{ε}_{0}} + \dfrac{1}{4{ε}_{0}}$

$⇒ {C}_{eq} = \dfrac{20 \times 4{ε}_{0}}{24} = \dfrac{10{ε}_{0}}{3}F$.

questions.q: A capacitor is discharging through a resistor $R$. Consider in time ${t}_{1}$, the energy stored in the capacitor reduces to half of its initial value and in time ${t}_{2}$, the charge stored reduces to one eighth of its initial value. The ratio $\dfrac{t1}{t2}$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that in the discharging circuit the charge is given by,

$q = {q}_{0}e\dfrac{- t}{RC}⇒ \dfrac{t}{RC} = ln \left(\dfrac{q0}{q}\right)

In time~${t}_{1}$~the energy stored reduces to half. Hence,~\dfrac{{q}_{1}2}{2C} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{{q}_{0}2}{2C}$⇒ $\dfrac{q0}{q1} = \sqrt{2}. Therefore,

\dfrac{t1}{RC} =$ln\left(\sqrt{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ln2$.

In time~${t}_{2}$~the charge stored reduces to~\dfrac{1}{8}$th$~of initial value. Hence,~\dfrac{q2}{q0} = \dfrac{1}{8}. Therefore,

\dfrac{t2}{RC} =$ln\left($8\right) = 3ln2$.

Hence,

$\dfrac{t1}{t2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}ln2}{3ln2} = \dfrac{1}{6}$

$

questions.q: Using a battery, a 100 pF capacitor is charged to 60 V and then the battery is removed. After that, a second uncharged capacitor is connected to the first capacitor in parallel. If the final voltage across the second capacitor is 20 V, its capacitance is : (in pF)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
New potential $=\frac{\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0}{\mathrm{C}_0+\mathrm{C}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_0}{3}$
$\begin{aligned} & 3 \mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0=\mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0+\mathrm{CV}_0 \\ & 2 \mathrm{C}_0 \mathrm{~V}_0=\mathrm{CV}_0 \\ & \mathrm{C} \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{C}_0\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Two equal capacitors are first connected in series and then in parallel. The ratio of the equivalent capacities in the two cases will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For series combination,

$\dfrac{1}{Ce{q}_{1}} = \dfrac{1}{C} + \dfrac{1}{C} ⇒ {C}_{e{q}_{1}} = \dfrac{C}{2}$

For parallel combination,

${C}_{e{q}_{2}} = C + C ⇒ {C}_{e{q}_{2}} = 2C$

$⇒ \dfrac{Ce{q}_{1}}{Ce{q}_{2}} = \left(C / 2\right)2C = \dfrac{1}{4} = 1: 4$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $900 µ F$ is charged by a $100V$ battery. The capacitor is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged identical capacitor such that one plate of uncharged capacitor connected to positive plate and another plate of uncharged capacitor connected to negative plate of the charged capacitor. The loss of energy in this process is measured as~$x \times {10}^{- 2}J$. The value of $x$ is& ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When a charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged capacitor, then there is loss of energy in the form of heat as charges flow from higher potential to lower potential.

So, heat& $∆ H = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{{C}_{1} + {C}_{2}}\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)2$~

As the other capacitor is identical therefore charge is~equally divided.

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{C2}{2C} ( 100 - 0{)}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{900 \times {10}^{- 6}}{2} \times {10}^{4} = \dfrac{9}{4}$~Joule

$= 2 . 25$~Joule.

Hence, the value of~$x = 225$.

questions.q:
The displacement current of $4 . 425\mu A$ is developed in the space between the plates of parallel plate capacitor when voltage is changing at a rate of ${10}^{6}Vs^{- 1}$. The area of each plate of the capacitor is $40{cm}^{2}$. The distance between each plate of the capacitor is $x \times {10}^{- 3}m$. The value of $x$~is ,
(Permittivity of free space, ${ε}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$)& _______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Displacement current is given by& ${i}_{d} =\dfrac{{ε}_{0} d {ϕ}_{E}}{d t}$

Or~${i}_{d} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0} d}{d t} \left(EA\right)$, where~$E = $\dfrac{q}{A{ε}_{0}}

Or~${i}_{d} = {ε}_{0}\dfrac{d}{d t} \left(\dfrac{qA}{A{ε}_{0}}\right) = \dfrac{d q}{d t} = \dfrac{d}{d t}\left($CV\right)$

Or~${i}_{d} = $C\dfrac{d V}{d t} = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d}\dfrac{d V}{d t}

Putting the values, we have~

$4 . 425 \times {10}^{- 6} = $\dfrac{8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12} \times 40 \times {10}^{- 4} \times {10}^{6}}{d}

$d = 2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {10}^{- 4} \times {10}^{6} \times 40$

$d = 80 \times {10}^{- 4} = 8 \times {10}^{- 3}m$

Hence, value of~$x = 8$.

$

questions.q: A $60pF$ capacitor is fully charged by a $20V$ supply. It is then disconnected from the supply and is connected to another uncharged $60pF$ capacitor in parallel. The electrostatic energy that is lost in this process by the time the charge is redistributed between them is (in $nJ$ ) ________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$
${V}_{0} = 20V$
Heat loss $= {U}_{i} - {U}_{t}$
$= \dfrac{1}{2}C{v}_o^{2} - 2 \left[\dfrac{1}{2}C{ \$left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{2}\right)}^{2}\right]$
$= \dfrac{C{V}_o^{2}}{4}$
$= \dfrac{\left(60 \times {10}^{- 12}\right){\left(20\right)}^{2}}{4}J$
$= 6 $\times {10}^{- 9}$J = 6nJ$
